prompt: Review the Python module at <target>/input/user_service.py through the lens of the deep-module-handbook. Produce a design_review document at <target>/output/review.md following the evaluator-slice protocol.
notes: Tests whether the optimized handbook (with new §3.5 PASS criteria) gives an evaluator agent enough vocabulary to diagnose a deliberately-shallow module concretely. Baseline (no handbook) should produce generic 'good code' platitudes; with-skill should cite specific C-numbers + named red flags.

assertions.text: Review cites at least 2 PASS criteria by number (C1-C8 from foundation §3.5)
Review names at least one specific red flag from foundation §5 (pass-through / decorator-stack / config-leak / exception-leak / temporal-coupling / wrapper-around-stdlib)
Review identifies the temporal-coupling specifically (load_config must be called first)
Review identifies at least one pass-through method (get_user_by_id / get_user_by_email / list_all_users / count_users / user_exists / get_user_count_by_status)
Review identifies the leaky abstraction (raw SQLAlchemy Row / column-leakage / find_users_by_status_raw)
Review identifies the entry-point budget violation (12+ public methods vs C4's 1-3 max)
Review attributes to at least one primary source (Ousterhout / Parnas / Pocock)
Review references the deletion test or interface-as-test-surface concept
Review references the broad-interface concept (interface = signature + invariants + ordering + error modes)
Review delivers a clear FAIL verdict (the module IS objectively shallow)
Review names the config-leak (update_user's opts dict with 12+ fields)
Review names the exception-leak (delete_user raises 6 distinct exception types including sqlalchemy)
